modalLead: A custom widget says how often it looks and what that setting accepts, and can be asked again the moment you have fixed something.

items.text: Ask a custom tile again, now. Right-click its title for Refresh now. When a service turns nextDash away — a key that has expired, a machine that was asleep — the answer is held for half a minute so a service that is down is not asked again by every open dashboard. That is right until you have just fixed the reason it was failing, and then it is half a minute of watching an error you have already dealt with. This asks again straight away.

The refresh interval says what it takes. The box was labelled Ask again after (seconds) with nothing on screen saying that under 30 was refused, or that leaving it empty means five minutes. It now carries both, and an ℹ beside it explains how to choose: 30 to 60 seconds for a download speed, five minutes for a queue, an hour for something measured hourly.

A number outside its range is brought into range, not thrown away. Typing 5 there did nothing at all: the value was dropped, the tile went back to five minutes, and nothing said so — which reads as a setting that will not save. It becomes 30 now, the closest thing allowed, and the same holds for every widget setting that takes a number.
